To make indistinct or hazy, to obscure or dim.

examples.text: to blur a photograph (by moving the camera while taking it)

glosses: To smear, stain or smudge.

examples.text: to blur a manuscript (by handling it while damp)

glosses: To become indistinct.
To cause imperfection of vision in; to dim; to darken.

examples.text: His eyes are blurred with the lightning's glare.

glosses: To sully; to stain; to blemish, as reputation.

examples.text: Sarcasms may eclipse thine own, / But cannot blur my lost renown.

glosses: To transfer the input focus away from.

examples.text: Then give this box focus to blur the first one: […]
These form elements need to have an onFocus event handler to blur the current focus.
Blurring one window and focusing on another window yields the same result of sending the window to the back of the pile.
A manual way to blur a text object is to press the Tab key, which advances focus to the next field in order and removes it from the current field (blurring it).

glosses: To use a sign, image, expression, etc. sufficiently close to a trademarked one that it causes confusion between them.
A smear, smudge or blot.
Something that appears hazy or indistinct.

examples.text: The surroundings went by in a blur.

Maccario, it was evident, did not care to take the risk of blundering upon a picket, and a man led them by twisting paths until at last the hacienda rose blackly before them. Appleby could see it dimly, a blur of shadowy buildings with the ridge of roof parapet alone cutting hard and sharp against the clearing sky.

The fightback when it came was in the [Roger] Federer fashion: unfussy, filled with classy strokes from the back with perfectly timed interventions at the net that confounded his opponent. The third set passed in a bit of a blur, the fourth, which led to the second tie-break, was the most dramatic of the match.

glosses: Haziness, blurriness.

examples.text: Unfortunately, a small artificial pupil also tends to increase the amount of diffraction somewhat, but this increase in blur is considerably smaller than the decrease that results from the control of other factors.
The second option (right-hand page) features a sharp background and a cyclist who appears as a smudge of blur.
Selectively applying blur to the edges can give the impression of a toy camera or a tilt-shift lens.

glosses: A moral stain or blot.

examples.text: […]with her raillyng sette a great blurre on myne honesty

glosses: Lacking awareness; clueless or confused.

examples.text: Even if you don't know, just pretend as if you know-lah Mike. You are embarrassing me you know. If you are so blur like this, how to accept you as my sidekick man?
If a Singaporean gets frustrated at your stupidity, he can scold you for being blur as sotong (clueless as a squid).

glosses: Weak; insipid; tasteless.

examples.text:
1825, Francis Jeffrey, Lord Jeffrey, review of Theodric by Thomas Campbell
Passages that are somewhat fade.
His masculine taste gave him a sense of something fade and ludicrous.

glosses: A golf shot that curves intentionally to the player's right (if they are right-handed) or to the left (if left-handed).

examples.text: If you confine yourself to hitting straight shots while you are developing your golf swing, you are less likely to develop a preference for hitting a fade or a draw.

glosses: A haircut where the hair is short or shaved on the sides of the head and longer on top. See also high-top fade and low fade.
A fight.
A gradual decrease in the brightness of a shot or the volume of sound or music (as a means of cutting to a new scene or starting a new song).
The act of disappearing from a place so as not to be found; covert departure.

examples.text: Ace could have done a fade. Instead, he gathered all his courage — which was not inconsiderable, even in his middle age — and went to see the Flying Corson Brothers.

glosses: To hit the ball with the shot called a fade.

examples.text: The Golden Bear faded the ball from left to right with great consistency, so he seldom had to worry about trouble on the left.

glosses: To grow weak; to lose strength; to decay; to perish gradually; to wither, as a plant.

examples.text: The earth mourneth and fadeth away.

glosses: To lose freshness, color, or brightness; to become faint in hue or tint; hence, to be wanting in color.

examples.text: [flowers] that never fade

The half-dozen pieces […] were painted white and carved with festoons of flowers, birds and cupids. To display them the walls had been tinted a vivid blue which had now faded, but the carpet, which had evidently been stored and recently relaid, retained its original turquoise.

glosses: To sink away; to disappear gradually; to grow dim; to vanish.

examples.text: The milkman's whistling faded into the distance.
He makes a swanlike end, / Fading in music.

1856, Eleanor Marx-Aveling (translator), Gustave Flaubert, Madame Bovary, Part III Chapter XI,
A strange thing was that Bovary, while continually thinking of Emma, was forgetting her. He grew desperate as he felt this image fading from his memory in spite of all efforts to retain it. Yet every night he dreamt of her; it was always the same dream. He drew near her, but when he was about to clasp her she fell into decay in his arms.

So many people have come and gone
Their faces fade as the years go by

They say your love will surely fade girl
When things go wrong and trouble calls
And with that, I think we'll leave 2021's tail lamp to fade into the distance.

glosses: To cause to fade.

examples.text: I tried to get some bets that y'all were fixin' to get married but nobody would fade me.
